text: Youna Kang[4][5] (born 27 February 1990), known online as CodeMiko and alias The Technician, is a South Korean-American Twitch streamer and YouTuber. She is best known for her live streams on Twitch, where she interviews other streamers, content creators, and internet personalities as her virtual persona CodeMiko,[6] and for advancing interactivity in VTuber technology.[7] Kang created the CodeMiko persona using Unreal Engine, a motion capture suit from Xsens, motion capture gloves from Manus VR, and a facial tracking helmet from MOCAP Design.[a][b][7] The avatar consists of 36,000 polygons, modeled in Autodesk Maya and textured using Adobe Substance. Originally developed alone, the project is now managed by a team including an engineer, an artist / animator / rigger,[8] a publicist, a personal assistant, and a manager.[9] Kang now leads development efforts in broadcasting and idea generation, focusing on introducing new standards of interactivity with her audience.[8] CodeMiko's virtual environment is quasi-interactive, allowing viewers to influence the avatar and surroundings through live chat or donations.[7] Kang conceived the idea for CodeMiko while working at Nickelodeon.[8] After being laid off due to the COVID-19 pandemic,[9] she transitioned to full-time streaming.[8] Early earnings were around $300 per month, insufficient to cover rent,[8] and she incurred over $20,000 in debt to purchase the necessary equipment, including the Xsens Mo-cap suit,[10] which she has credited as pivotal to her success despite poor risk management.[10][9] Since the project's success, she can now afford a comfortable living.[9] Her streaming breakthrough occurred in 2021, following a viral tweet on Twitter[11] and going viral on r/LiveStreamFails on Reddit.[10] The CodeMiko avatar has an in-universe backstory as a video game character without a game, who always wanted to be in a mainstream video game but failed due to her 'Glitch'—a narrative arc similar to Vanellope von Schweetz from Wreck-It Ralph. She was forced into minor roles, like a bush in The Last of Us, mirroring the struggles of a Hollywood actress seeking any role in a film, and for her, any video game.[10] She eventually found her place in Kang’s Unreal Engine project, becoming a Twitch streamer and currently roaming various game worlds, including the world of dead memes and The Sims. The avatar is aware of the Technician and frequently breaks the fourth wall, both indirectly through cross-over interviews such as CodeMiko interviewing The Technician,[13] and directly via augmented reality.[14] The character's "glitchiness" is expressed through occasional transitions into her evil alter ego, "Glitch," who replaces her pink-haired avatar with a semi-transparent, Matrix-inspired digital rain avatar and speaks with a deeper, hoarser voice via a voice changer, often being profane and offensive. It was previously believed that CodeMiko was initially released under the name 'mikoglitch',[15] but in a VOD,[16] Youna clarified this was false and explained that 'mikoglitch' was created to circumvent a temporary shadow ban on her 'CodeMiko' channel. The interview format has been likened to the 1990s animated parody show Space Ghost Coast to Coast.[8] Kang described Glitch as "kind of stupid, unfiltered, and not afraid to say whatever is on her mind or what she sees."[8] In 2021, CodeMiko participated in PogChamps 3, placing last with four losses and zero wins, alongside streamer Myth,[17] and was coached by WGM Anna Rudolf[18] and Andrea Botez.[19] Kang developed "TOS PTSD" after unintentionally violating Twitch's terms of service, resulting in bans, leading to economic anxiety and seeking help from psychiatrist Alok Kanojia on stream.[8][20] She expressed concern about Twitch's proposed "Brand Safety Score" system, fearing her X-rated humor might make her content unsuitable for advertisers and threaten her income, though she later noted her concerns lessened due to brand sponsorships.[22][9] The project has received positive reception, with Kotaku calling CodeMiko "The Future Of Streaming"[8] and Designboom stating she is "Revolutionizing the digital space."[7] The Financial Times reported her content as signaling "The next frontier of digital entertainment",[12] and Quartz described her as "The talk show host of the future."[23] The Verge noted she is "reshaping the Twitch landscape in her image."[10] The project has also attracted interest from producers of sexually explicit content.[12]
